statements.text: Grand River Transit estimates that running its buses and trains (operations, maintenance, fuel and wages) would cost $262 million a year by 2034 to deliver its whole Business Plan, up from $195 million in 2025, in 2025 dollars.
The plan lists $798 million of major transit capital projects for 2025 to 2035; about $544 million of it was already in the approved capital program.

citations.quote: The GRT Business Plan identifies $798 million in major transit capital projects over the 2025–2035 timeframe
approximately $544 million is currently accommodated within the approved 2025-2034 Transit Capital Program

statements.text: These estimates leave out ION Stage 2 and Kitchener Central Station.

citations.quote: Excludes ION Stage 2 and Kitchener Central Station

statements.text: Each year's budget decides how much of the plan goes ahead.

citations.quote: subject to Regional Council’s annual Plan and Budget process

statements.text: After fares and other revenue, GRT expects the net operating cost to reach $199 million a year by 2034, up from $149 million.
Separately, the Region's 10-year capital plan sets aside $2.05 billion for light rail to Cambridge (ION Stage 2), starting with $85 million in 2027.
In 2026, transit took $516 of an average household's regional property tax.

assumptions.label: Years counted
assumptions.why: The plan runs to 2034. Counting 25 years (2025–2049) also shows the 15 years after it is built out, when the bigger network keeps costing money to run.

assumptions.label: Discount rate
assumptions.why: At 0% every year's dollar counts the same. A higher rate counts future dollars for less, as many public-sector cost studies do (3% is common).

assumptions.label: Yearly operating spending once the plan is built
assumptions.why: GRT's 2034 estimate for the full plan, in 2025 dollars, without debt payments (those pay for the capital already counted). The chart climbs in a straight line from $195 million in 2025 because the plan gives only the start and the end; moving this slider sets every year to one amount.

assumptions.label: Bus replacement after 2034
assumptions.why: After 2034 we assume buses keep being replaced at the plan's pace: $487 million of fleet over ten years, about $48.7 million a year. No document gives spending after 2034.

assumptions.label: Capital cost overrun
assumptions.why: Large transit projects often cost more than first estimated, and GRT calls these figures demonstrative. Slide to see what an overrun adds.

assumptions.label: Households sharing the cost
assumptions.why: 222,426 households lived in Waterloo Region at the 2021 Census (Statistics Canada). There are more now. Businesses pay too, so this is a rough share per home, not a bill.

method: Lifecycle cost = capital in the years it is spent + operating and maintenance in each year of service + renewals in the years they fall + emissions × carbon price (none counted here), over the years shown, in today's dollars, undiscounted unless a discount rate is set. Built in code by lenses/cost from figures whose quotes were checked on their pages; everything else is a labelled assumption.
inputNotes: Capital: $798 million (cited) spread evenly over 2025–2034, the ten years of the plan's capital table (assumption: the plan gives no year-by-year split).
Operating: $195 million in 2025 and $262 million in 2034 (cited), straight line in between (assumption), then held at $262 million in 2025 dollars.
Maintenance is inside GRT's operating line (operations, maintenance, fuel, wages), so it is not counted twice.
Debt payments and transfers to reserves ($39 million rising to $52 million) are left out because they pay for capital that is already counted.
Renewal: bus replacement after 2034 at $48.7 million a year, the plan's fleet budget divided by ten (assumption).
Emissions are not counted: no document gives Grand River Transit's own emissions, so no carbon cost is added.
Revenue (fares, gas tax, advertising) is not subtracted: this is the cost of the service, not what taxpayers pay after fares.
unknowns: What ION Stage 2 (light rail to Cambridge) will cost to run each year: no operating estimate is in these documents.
What the 2027 budget will fund of the plan: the draft budget is not public until December 2026.
Bus replacement and garage costs after 2035.
